characters.name: Bernard
characters.personality: precise, a little talkative, proud of his old silk-weavers' building

characters.name: Sylvie
characters.personality: quick, friendly, has seen every kind of parcel

characters.name: Inès
characters.personality: patient, apologetic, keen to fix things

characters.name: Romain
characters.personality: energetic, encouraging, says tu to everyone from the first minute

notes: Vous with the landlord, the post office clerk, the shop assistant, the doctor and the airline agent; the running coach says tu, as is normal in French sports clubs, and the learner's lines to him avoid both tu and vous. Please confirm.

The learner's lines keep the masculine default of chapters 1–3 (arrivé); feminine forms are in the notes. The learner now lives on the slopes of the Croix-Rousse (rue Burdeau), where the flat of mission 1 is.
Wordings to check first: « Dès le premier du mois », « Je vous règle par carte. », « Je vous la rembourse ? », « C’est clair pour vous ? », « Que se passe-t-il ? » from an airline agent.

Facts to verify: 800 euros a month charges comprises for a flat in the Croix-Rousse, Colissimo prices and delays to Canada (42 euros, 65 euros express, for 2 kg), the 30-euro GP visit, a running club at 100 euros a year, the London–Lyon flight.

titles.en: Visiting a flat in the Croix-Rousse

scene.en: A bright flat on the third floor of an old silk-weavers' building in the Croix-Rousse, with no lift; Bernard, the owner, shows you round.

lines.text: Entrez, je vous en prie. Voilà le salon.
lines.pron: Je vous en prie: zhuh voo-zahn PREE. Salon: sah-LON.

en.m: Come in, please. Here's the living room.
en.n: Je vous en prie = please, go ahead (it also means 'you're welcome'). French counts floors from le rez-de-chaussée, so le troisième étage is the US fourth floor.
en.l: enter, I you of-it pray. there-is the living-room

lines.text: Il est vraiment lumineux, ce salon !

en.m: This living room is really bright!
en.n: Lumineux (full of light) is the word every flat advert uses. The old canut flats of the Croix-Rousse are known for high ceilings and tall windows.
en.l: it is really luminous, this living-room

lines.text: Et le loyer, c’est combien par mois ?

en.m: And how much is the rent a month?
en.n: Le loyer = the rent. Naming the topic first, then asking c’est combien ?, is the natural spoken order.
en.l: and the rent, it is how-much by month

lines.text: Huit cents euros, charges comprises.
lines.pron: Huit cents euros: wee sahn-zuh-ROH. Comprises: kon-PREEZ.

en.m: Eight hundred euros, including service charges.
en.n: Charges comprises = service charges included (building upkeep, often water and heating); charges en plus = on top of the rent.
en.l: eight hundreds euros, charges included

lines.text: Où est la machine à laver ?
lines.pron: Machine à laver: mah-SHEEN ah lah-VAY.

en.m: Where's the washing machine?
en.n: Une machine à laver (a machine to wash). À + infinitive says what a thing is for: une salle à manger, a dining room.
en.l: where is the machine to wash

lines.text: Et le métro, c’est loin ?
lines.pron: Loin: lwan, nasal, no n sound.

en.m: And is the metro far?
en.n: Answers you may hear: c’est tout près (it's very close), c’est à deux pas (it's two steps away).
en.l: and the metro, it is far

lines.text: La machine est dans la cuisine, et le métro à cinq minutes.

en.m: The machine's in the kitchen, and the metro's five minutes away.
en.n: French drops a repeated verb just as English can: le métro (est) à cinq minutes. À + time = away: c’est à dix minutes à pied.
en.l: the machine is in the kitchen, and the metro at five minutes

lines.text: Il est libre à partir de quand ?
lines.pron: Libre: leebr. À partir de: ah par-TEER duh.

en.m: When is it available from?
en.n: Libre = free, available, for a flat, a table or a person. À partir de = from, starting from.
en.l: it is free at to-leave from when

lines.text: Dès le premier du mois. Mais attention, le voisin joue du piano !

en.m: From the first of the month. But be warned, the neighbour plays the piano!
en.n: Dès = from, as early as. Jouer du + instrument: jouer du piano, de la guitare; but jouer au + sport: jouer au foot.
en.l: from the first of-the month. but attention, the neighbour plays some piano

lines.text: Pas de problème, j’aime la musique. Je le prends !

en.m: No problem, I like music. I'll take it!
en.n: Le stands for l’appartement. Next step: you sign le bail, the lease, and make l’état des lieux, the check-in inventory.
en.l: not of problem, I love the music. I it take

lines.text: Le dépôt de garantie, c’est combien ?

en.m: How much is the deposit?
en.n: Le dépôt de garantie, often called la caution, is the security deposit: by law at most one month's rent for an unfurnished flat.
en.l: the deposit of guarantee, it is how-much

scene.en: The post office on a busy Saturday morning; you are sending a small box of presents to your family in Toronto, and the clerk offers a faster option.

lines.text: Bonjour, je voudrais envoyer ce colis.
lines.pron: Envoyer: ahn-vwah-YAY. Colis: koh-LEE, silent s.

en.m: Hello, I'd like to send this parcel.
en.n: Je voudrais + infinitive = I'd like to. Un colis = a parcel; une lettre = a letter. La Poste also sells ready-made boxes.
en.l: good-day, I would-like to-send this parcel

lines.text: Très bien. C’est pour quel pays ?

en.m: Fine. Which country is it going to?
en.n: Quel agrees with its noun: quel pays, quelle ville, quels jours.
en.l: very well. it is for which country

lines.text: Pour le Canada, à Toronto.
lines.pron: Canada: kah-nah-DAH, stressed at the end.

en.m: To Canada, to Toronto.
en.n: Countries take an article: le Canada, la France, les États-Unis. Going there: au Canada, en France, aux États-Unis; but à before a city: à Toronto.
en.l: for the Canada, at Toronto

lines.text: Posez-le sur la balance, s’il vous plaît.

en.m: Put it on the scales, please.
en.n: In a command, le comes after the verb with a hyphen: posez-le. Une balance = a pair of scales.
en.l: put-it on the scales, if it you pleases

lines.text: Deux kilos, ça fait combien ?

en.m: How much is it for two kilos?
en.n: Ça fait combien ? = how much does that come to? France weighs in kilos and grams: un kilo, cinq cents grammes.
en.l: two kilos, that makes how-much

lines.text: Quarante-deux euros, ou soixante-cinq en express.

en.m: Forty-two euros, or sixty-five by express.
en.n: Soixante (60) is the last regular ten: seventy is soixante-dix, 'sixty-ten'. Express costs more but arrives sooner.
en.l: forty-two euros, or sixty-five in express

lines.text: Et ça met combien de temps ?
lines.pron: Met: meh. Temps: tahn, silent p and s.

en.m: And how long does it take?
en.n: Mettre du temps (to put time) = to take time: ça met une semaine. Combien de + noun = how much, how many.
en.l: and that puts how-much of time

lines.text: Une semaine environ, ou trois jours en express.

en.m: About a week, or three days by express.
en.n: Environ (about) can come before or after the amount: environ une semaine, une semaine environ.
en.l: a week about, or three days in express

lines.text: Le moins cher, s’il vous plaît. Ce n’est pas urgent.

en.m: The cheaper one, please. It's not urgent.
en.n: Le moins cher = the least expensive; le plus rapide = the fastest.
en.l: the less expensive, if it you pleases. it not is not urgent

lines.text: Je vous règle par carte.

en.m: I'll pay you by card.
en.n: Régler (to settle) is a polite verb for paying at a counter: je vous règle par carte, en espèces. Payer works too.
en.l: I you settle by card

lines.text: C’est pour envoyer un colis au Canada.

en.m: I'm here to send a parcel to Canada.
en.n: C’est pour + infinitive = I'm here to: the usual way to state your business at a counter. To collect a parcel: c’est pour retirer un colis.
en.l: it is for to-send a parcel to-the Canada

scene.en: The customer service desk of a home appliance shop on the rue de la République; the kettle you bought there last week doesn't heat.

lines.text: Bonjour, qu’est-ce que je peux faire pour vous ?

en.m: Hello, what can I do for you?
en.n: The standard opening at a service desk. Answer with bonjour first: in a French shop, the greeting always comes before the problem.
en.l: good-day, what is-it that I can to-do for you

lines.text: Bonjour, cette bouilloire ne chauffe pas.

en.m: Hello, this kettle doesn't heat up.
en.n: Une bouilloire = a kettle (from bouillir, to boil). Chauffer = to heat. For anything that doesn't work at all: ça ne marche pas.
en.l: good-day, this kettle not heats not

lines.text: Je l’ai achetée ici la semaine dernière.

en.m: I bought it here last week.
en.n: With l’ (the kettle, feminine) placed before avoir, the participle takes an e in writing: je l’ai achetée. It sounds just like acheté.
en.l: I it-have bought here the week last

lines.text: Je suis désolée. Vous avez le ticket de caisse ?
lines.pron: Ticket de caisse: tee-KAY duh KESS.

en.m: I'm sorry. Do you have the receipt?
en.n: Le ticket de caisse = the till receipt; un reçu is more formal. Shops usually ask for it before any refund or exchange.
en.l: I am sorry. you have the ticket of till

lines.text: Ce n’est pas grave. Oui, le voici.

en.m: That's all right. Yes, here it is.
en.n: Ce n’est pas grave (it's not serious) = no problem, that's all right. Le voici = here it is; la voici for a feminine noun.
en.l: it not is not serious. yes, it here-is

lines.text: Merci. Je vous la rembourse ?

en.m: Thank you. Shall I refund it?
en.n: Rembourser = to refund. A present-tense statement with a rising voice works as an offer: je vous la rembourse ? = shall I refund it for you?
en.l: thanks. I to-you it refund

lines.text: Vous pouvez plutôt me l’échanger ?

en.m: Could you exchange it for me instead?
en.n: Plutôt = instead, rather. Two pronouns go in this order: me l’échanger = exchange it for me.
en.l: you can rather to-me it-exchange

lines.text: Bien sûr. Tenez, celle-ci est neuve.

en.m: Of course. Here you are, this one is brand new.
en.n: Tenez = here you are, as you hand something over. Neuf, neuve = brand new; nouveau, nouvelle = new, another one.
en.l: well sure. hold, this-one-here is new

lines.text: Merci, vous êtes très aimable.

en.m: Thank you, that's very kind of you.
en.n: Vous êtes très aimable is a warm, polite thank-you for good service.
en.l: thanks, you are very kind

lines.text: Elle ne marche pas du tout.

en.m: It doesn't work at all.
en.n: Marcher (to walk) also means 'to work' for machines: ça marche ! = it works! Pas du tout = not at all. Elle because une bouilloire is feminine.
en.l: she not walks not at-all

lines.text: Je peux en avoir une autre ?

en.m: Can I have another one?
en.n: En = of them: je peux en avoir une autre ? = can I have another (of them)? Say un autre for a masculine noun.
en.l: I can of-them to-have an other

scene.en: A GP's surgery in your neighbourhood; you have had a sore throat and a slight fever for two days, and Dr Moreau has a slot at 5 p.m.

lines.text: Bonjour, docteur.

en.m: Good afternoon, doctor.
en.n: Docteur is how you address a doctor; when you talk about one, say un médecin. From about 6 p.m., say bonsoir instead.
en.l: good-day, doctor

lines.text: Bonjour, asseyez-vous. Qu’est-ce qui vous amène ?

en.m: Hello, have a seat. What brings you here?
en.n: Qu’est-ce qui vous amène ? (what brings you?) is the doctor's usual first question. Asseyez-vous = sit down.
en.l: good-day, sit-yourself. what is-it that you brings

lines.text: J’ai mal à la gorge, et un peu de fièvre.

en.m: I have a sore throat and a slight fever.
en.n: Avoir mal à + body part: mal à la gorge (throat), mal à la tête (head), mal au ventre (stomach). Fever is measured in Celsius: 38 °C counts as fever.
en.l: I have bad at the throat, and a little of fever

lines.text: Depuis combien de temps ?

en.m: For how long?
en.n: Depuis = since, for. French uses the present with depuis where English needs 'have had': j’ai mal depuis deux jours.
en.l: since how-much of time

lines.text: Depuis deux jours, à peu près.
lines.pron: À peu près: ah puh PREH.

en.m: For about two days.
en.n: À peu près = about, roughly. You can also give a starting point: depuis samedi, depuis hier soir.
en.l: since two days, at little near

lines.text: C’est une petite angine. Je vous prescris un sirop.
lines.pron: Angine: ahn-ZHEEN. Sirop: see-ROH, silent p.

en.m: It's a mild throat infection. I'm prescribing you a syrup.
en.n: False friend: une angine is a throat infection, not angina. Take the prescription, l’ordonnance, to any pharmacy.
en.l: it is a little throat-infection. I you prescribe a syrup

lines.text: Je le prends combien de fois par jour ?
lines.pron: Fois: fwah. Par jour: par ZHOOR.

en.m: How many times a day do I take it?
en.n: Combien de fois = how many times. Une fois, deux fois counts occasions; une heure is the time on the clock.
en.l: I it take how-much of times by day

lines.text: Trois fois par jour, après les repas. C’est clair pour vous ?

en.m: Three times a day, after meals. Is that clear for you?
en.n: C’est clair pour vous ? = is that clear? Doctors and pharmacists check that you have understood a dosage; don't be shy to ask again.
en.l: three times by day, after the meals. it is clear for you

lines.text: Oui, c’est clair. Trois fois par jour.

en.m: Yes, that's clear. Three times a day.
en.n: Repeating the key information back is the best way to show, and to check, that you have understood.
en.l: yes, it is clear. three times by day

lines.text: Merci beaucoup, docteur. Au revoir !

en.m: Thank you very much, doctor. Goodbye!
en.n: A GP visit costs 30 euros; with a carte Vitale, the French health card, most of it is paid back by the Sécurité sociale.
en.l: thanks much, doctor. to-the seeing-again

lines.text: J’ai très mal quand j’avale.

en.m: It really hurts when I swallow.
en.n: Avaler = to swallow. Quand + present = when: j’ai mal quand je parle, quand je mange.
en.l: I have very bad when I swallow

scene.en: A running club that meets on the banks of the Rhône; Romain, the coach, says tu to everyone, and the first month is free.

lines.text: Bonjour ! Les entraînements, c’est quels jours ?

en.m: Hello! Which days are the training sessions?
en.n: Un entraînement = a training session. Quels jours ? = which days? Topic first, then the question: very common in spoken French.
en.l: good-day! the trainings, it is which days

lines.text: Le mardi et le jeudi, à dix-neuf heures.
lines.pron: Dix-neuf heures: deez-nuh-VUHR; the f of neuf sounds like v before heures.

en.m: Tuesdays and Thursdays, at 7 p.m.
en.n: Le mardi = on Tuesdays, every week. Dix-neuf heures = 7 p.m.: clubs and timetables use the 24-hour clock.
en.l: the Tuesday and the Thursday, at nineteen hours

lines.text: Et l’inscription, c’est combien ?

en.m: And how much is it to join?
en.n: L’inscription = signing up, and the fee for it. Most French clubs charge a yearly fee, la cotisation, often paid in September.
en.l: and the inscription, it is how-much

lines.text: Le premier mois est gratuit, puis c’est cent euros par an.

en.m: The first month is free, then it's a hundred euros a year.
en.n: Gratuit = free of charge; libre = free as in available. Cent links to euros with a t sound.
en.l: the first month is free, then it is hundred euros by year

lines.text: Je peux venir faire un essai jeudi ?

en.m: Can I come and try it out on Thursday?
en.n: Faire un essai = to have a trial session. Jeudi without le = this Thursday.
en.l: I can to-come to-do a try Thursday

lines.text: Bien sûr ! Tu cours combien de kilomètres, en général ?

en.m: Of course! How many kilometres do you usually run?
en.n: In sports clubs everyone says tu, the coach included. Courir: je cours, tu cours, il court; the final letters are silent.
en.l: well sure! you run how-many of kilometres, in general

lines.text: Environ cinq. J’adore courir au bord de l’eau !
lines.pron: Courir: koo-REER. Au bord de l’eau: oh BOR duh LOH.

en.m: About five. I love running by the water!
en.n: Au bord de = at the edge of, by: au bord de l’eau, au bord de la mer. Cinq stands alone: kilomètres is understood.
en.l: about five. I adore to-run at-the edge of the water

lines.text: Super ! Rendez-vous jeudi au pont de la Guillotière.

en.m: Great! See you Thursday at the Guillotière bridge.
en.n: Rendez-vous ! = let's meet; un rendez-vous is also an appointment. The Pont de la Guillotière is one of the bridges over the Rhône.
en.l: super! meeting Thursday at-the bridge of the Guillotière

lines.text: Parfait, à jeudi, dix-neuf heures !

en.m: Perfect, see you Thursday at seven!
en.n: À + day = see you then: à jeudi, à lundi. Repeating the time is a simple way to confirm a plan.
en.l: perfect, to Thursday, nineteen hours

lines.text: Est-ce que je peux juste regarder, la première fois ?

en.m: Can I just watch the first time?
en.n: Est-ce que je peux… ? is a little more careful than je peux… ?. Juste = just, only, in everyday speech.
en.l: is-it that I can just to-watch, the first time

lines.text: Courir, ça me fait du bien.

en.m: Running does me good.
en.n: Ça me fait du bien = it does me good. Naming the activity first, then picking it up with ça, is typical of spoken French.
en.l: to-run, that to-me does some good

scene.en: The baggage desk at Lyon Saint-Exupéry airport; your flight from London landed an hour ago, but your big blue suitcase never came out.

lines.text: Excusez-moi, c’est ici pour les bagages perdus ?

en.m: Excuse me, is this the place for lost luggage?
en.n: Les bagages is plural in French where English says 'luggage': mes bagages = my luggage, un bagage = one bag.
en.l: excuse-me, it is here for the luggages lost

lines.text: Oui, c’est bien ici. Que se passe-t-il ?
lines.pron: Que se passe-t-il: kuh suh pahss-TEEL.

en.m: Yes, this is the right place. What's the problem?
en.n: Que se passe-t-il ? is the formal form of qu’est-ce qui se passe ?: verb and subject swap, and -t- is added between two vowels.
en.l: yes, it is well here. what itself passes-t-it

lines.text: Ma valise n’est pas arrivée.

en.m: My suitcase didn't arrive.
en.n: Arriver takes être in the passé composé, so the participle agrees with the subject: ma valise n’est pas arrivée. It sounds the same as arrivé.
en.l: my suitcase not is not arrived

lines.text: Je suis arrivé de Londres il y a une heure.
lines.pron: Londres: LONDR. Il y a une heure: eel-yah ün UHR.

en.m: I arrived from London an hour ago.
en.n: Il y a + time = ago: il y a une heure, il y a deux jours. A woman writes arrivée; it sounds the same.
en.l: I am arrived from London there-has an hour

lines.text: Je suis désolée, elle est restée à Londres.

en.m: I'm sorry, it stayed behind in London.
en.n: False friend: rester means to stay, to remain, not 'to rest'. Elle est restée: rester takes être too.
en.l: I am sorry, she is stayed at London

lines.text: Quand est-ce que je vais la récupérer ?
lines.pron: Quand est-ce que: kahn-TESS-kuh; the d sounds like t. Récupérer: ray-kü-pay-RAY.

en.m: When will I get it back?
en.n: Récupérer = to get back, to collect. La stands for la valise and goes before the infinitive: je vais la récupérer.
en.l: when is-it that I go it to-recover

lines.text: Demain matin. On vous la livre à quelle adresse ?

en.m: Tomorrow morning. Which address shall we deliver it to?
en.n: Livrer = to deliver. Spelling trap: adresse has one d and two s in French, the reverse of English 'address'.
en.l: tomorrow morning. one to-you it delivers at which address

lines.text: Chez moi, s’il vous plaît : 12, rue Burdeau.
lines.pron: Chez moi: shay MWAH. Douze: dooz.

en.m: To my home, please: 12 rue Burdeau.
en.n: Chez moi = at my place, to my home. A French address starts with the number, then the street: 12, rue Burdeau, 69001 Lyon.
en.l: at-home-of me, if it you pleases: 12, street Burdeau

lines.text: C’est noté. Voici votre numéro de dossier.

en.m: That's noted. Here's your file number.
en.n: C’est noté = noted, that's done. Keep le numéro de dossier (the file reference) to track your suitcase online.
en.l: it is noted. here-is your number of file

lines.text: Merci beaucoup, madame. Bonne soirée !

en.m: Thank you very much. Have a good evening!
en.n: Bonne soirée = have a nice evening; bonne journée during the day. Adding madame or monsieur makes a thank-you warmer.
en.l: thanks much, madam. good evening

lines.text: Mon sac à dos n’est pas sur le tapis.
lines.pron: Sac à dos: sah-kah-DOH. Tapis: tah-PEE.

en.m: My backpack isn't on the carousel.
en.n: Le tapis (à bagages) = the baggage carousel; un tapis is also a rug. Un sac à dos (a bag on the back) = a backpack.
en.l: my bag at back not is not on the carpet
